He was drafted by the [[Utah Jazz]] following his freshman season at the [[University of Kentucky]]. Lyles has also played for the [[Denver Nuggets]], [[San Antonio Spurs]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==Early life== Trey Lyles was born in [[Saskatoon]], [[Saskatchewan]] to an American father and Canadian mother, and moved to [[Indianapolis]], [[Indiana]] at the age of seven.{{Cite web|url=https://thejnotes.com/2015/06/28/who-is-new-jazz-man-trey-lyles/|title=Who Is New Jazz Man Trey Lyles?|date=June 29, 2015|website=The J-Notes}} ==High school career== [[File:20140402 MCDAAG Trey Lyles rebound (1).JPG|thumb|right|upright|Lyles in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Entering his senior year of high school in Indianapolis, Lyles was ranked as one of the best high school basketball players in the U.S. and was recruited heavily by [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]]. Lyles originally committed to [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] in September 2010 during his freshman year of high school, but then later decommitted in August 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/recruiting/eye-on-college-basketball-recruiting/19748489/top10-forward-trey-lyles-decommits-from-indiana|title=Top-10 forward Trey Lyles decommits from Indiana|publisher=CBSsports.com|author= Borzello, Jeff|date=August 7, 2012|access-date=October 10, 2014}} Lyles signed a letter of intent on November 5, 2013, to play and study at the [[University of Kentucky]].{{cite web|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|title=Five-star Trey Lyles commits to Kentucky, gives Wildcats No. 1 class|publisher=CBSsports.com|date=November 5, 2013|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24191968/five-star-trey-lyles-commits-to-kentucky-gives-wildcats-no-1-class|access-date=August 5, 2014}} During his senior year of high school, Lyles averaged 23.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 3.5 assists and led [[Arsenal Technical High School|Arsenal Tech]] to the [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] Class 4A State Championship game with a 63–59 victory over [[Lake Central High School|Lake Central]].{{cite Lyles enrolled at Kentucky on June 12, 2014. Due to an unspecified leg injury, Lyles sat out [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky's]] six-game [[Exhibition game|exhibition]] series in [[Nassau, Bahamas]] from August 10 through August 17.{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/06/24/kentuckys-lyles-play-bahamas-basketball-tour/11313395/|title=Kentucky's Lyles won't play on Bahamas basketball tour|publisher=The Courier-Journal|date=June 24, 2014|access-date=October 10, 2014|author=Tucker, Kyle}} As a freshman, Lyles was named to the 2015 All-SEC Freshman Team and helped lead the Wildcats to a 2015 NCAA Final Four appearance. On April 9, 2015, Lyles along with Kentucky teammates [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], [[Aaron Harrison]], [[Dakari Johnson]], [[Devin Booker]], [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and [[Willie Cauley-Stein]] declared to enter their names into the [[2015 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2015–2017)=== On June 25, 2015, Lyles was selected with the 12th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-select-lyles-hanlan-2015-nba-draft|title=Jazz select Lyles, Hanlan in 2015 NBA Draft|date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}} He signed his rookie scale contract with the Jazz on July 7.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-2015-draft-pick-trey-lyles|title=Jazz Sign 2015 Draft Pick Trey Lyles|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2015|access-date=July 8, 2015}} Lyles averaged 3.0 points and 3.6 rebounds per game over the first two months of his rookie season. He began picking up his production with more steady minutes during the month of January, scoring in double figures for the first time on January 4 with 13 points against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/HOUUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Harden scores 30, Rockets rally for 93-91 win over Jazz|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2016}} On January 9, in a win over the [[Miami Heat]], he recorded 10 rebounds for the first time,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160109/MIAUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Hayward scores 34 points, Jazz defeat Heat 98-83|work=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2016|access-date=January 14, 2016}} and on January 14, he scored a then season-high 19 points in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160114/SACUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Gay scores 24 and hits game-winner, Kings top Jazz 103-101|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2016|access-date=January 14, 2016}} On February 3, he was named a [[Rising Stars Challenge]] participant at the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game|2016 NBA All-Star Weekend]], replacing the injured [[Nikola Mirotić]] on the World Team roster.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/trey-lyles-added-2016-bbva-compass-rising-stars-challenge|title=Trey Lyles Added to 2016 BBVA Compass Rising Stars Challenge|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2016}} On April 10, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 100–84 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160410/UTADEN/gameinfo.html|title=Jazz use 24-0 run in 3rd quarter to beat Nuggets 100-84|work=NBA.com|date=April 10, 2016|access-date=April 10, 2016}} ===Denver Nuggets (2017–2019)=== On June 22, 2017, Lyles was traded, along with the draft rights to [[Tyler Lydon]], to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Donovan Mitchell]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-lyles-lydon-from-utah|title=Nuggets Acquire Trey Lyles and Tyler Lydon from Utah in Draft-Night Trade|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2017}} On December 2, 2017, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 115–100 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975083|title=Murray, Barton lead Nuggets over Lakers, 115-100.|work=ESPN.com|date=December 2, 2017|access-date=December 2, 2017}} On December 10, 2017, he scored a career-high 25 points in a 126–116 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975138|title=Oladipo scores career-high 47 as Pacers beat Nuggets in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 10, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2017}} On January 5, 2018, he set a new career high with 26 points in a 99–91 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975320|title=Lyle scores career-high 26 as Nuggets beat Jazz 99-91|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2018}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2019–2021)=== On July 12, 2019, Lyles signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=SPURS SIGN TREY LYLES|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-trey-lyles|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 12, 2019|date=July 12, 2019}} On February 6, 2020, Lyles had a double-double, scoring a season-high 23 points while grabbing 10 rebounds and two steals in a 125–117 loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Spurs' Trey Lyles finding new life with third team|url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/Spurs-Trey-Lyles-finding-new-life-with-third-15039372.php|website=Express News|access-date=March 2, 2020|date=February 7, 2020}} On February 29, 2020, Lyles scored 20 points, nine rebounds, two assists, four steals, and one block in a 114–113 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite news|title=Spurs overcome shaky finish to beat Magic, 114-113|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/spurs-overcome-shaky-finish-to-beat-magic-114-113/2020/02/29/f6299158-5b72-11ea-8efd-0f904bdd8057_story.html?outputType=amp|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|access-date=March 3, 2020|date=February 29, 2020}} On March 2, 2020, Lyles got himself 20 points again, along with three rebounds, two assists, and one steal in a 116–111 loss against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite news|title=Brogdon scores 26, Pacers forced to rally late to beat Spurs|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/brogdon-scores-26-pacers-forced-to-rally-late-to-beat-spurs/2020/03/02/7a3dc7a0-5d05-11ea-ac50-18701e14e06d_story.html|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|access-date=March 3, 2020|date=March 2, 2020}} On July 15, 2020, Lyles was reported to have undergone an [[appendectomy]] and was expected to miss the remainder of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]].{{cite web|title=Spurs' Trey Lyles to miss restart with appendicitis|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/07/15/sna-antonio-spurs-trey-lyles-miss-restart-appendicitis-official-release|date=July 15, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 15, 2020}} ===Detroit Pistons (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Lyles signed a two-year, $5 million contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web | last=Gauruder | first=Dana | title=Trey Lyles Signs Two-Year Deal With Pistons | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2021-08-02 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/trey-lyles-agrees-to-two-year-deal-with-pistons.html | access-date=2025-12-09}} ===Sacramento Kings (2022–2025)=== On February 10, 2022, Lyles and [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]] were acquired by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a four-team trade that sent [[Marvin Bagley III]] to the Pistons.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-donte-divincenzo-josh-jackson-and-trey-lyles-four-team-deal|website=nba.com|title=Kings Acquire Donte DiVincenzo, Josh Jackson and Trey Lyles in Four-Team Deal|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}} On March 13, 2023, during a 133–124 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Lyles fouled and shoved Bucks forward [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]], who was taunting Lyles in the last few moments of the game. Bucks center [[Brook Lopez]] then confronted Lyles, and the two resulted in a scuffle. Both Lyles and Lopez were ejected from the game. Two days later, the NBA announced that Lyles had been suspended for one game without pay due to his role in the altercation.{{Cite web |title=Kings' Trey Lyles suspended and Bucks' Brook Lopez fined |url=https://pr.nba.com/trey-lyles-suspended-brook-lopez-fined/ |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=NBA Communications|date=March 15, 2023 }} ===Real Madrid (2025–2026)=== On September 10, 2025, Lyles signed a one-year, $3.2 million contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]; the contract also includes an NBA out clause.{{cite web |title=Official Announcement: Trey Lyles |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-trey-lyles-10-09-2025 |website=realmadrid.com |access-date=September 12, 2025 |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/trey-lyles-taking-basketball-talents-spain/ |website=KSR |access-date=September 8, 2025 |date=September 5, 2025}} On May 24, 2026, despite a 24–point and eight rebound performance from Lyles, Real Madrid lost the EuroLeague Final against [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] by 92–85.{{Cite web |title=Olympiacos crowned EuroLeague champions after thrilling tussle with Real Madrid |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/olympiacos-crowned-euroleague-champions-after-thrilling-tussle-with-real-madrid/}} On June 23, Lyles left Real Madrid.{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/trey-lyles-bids-farewell-to-real-madrid/|title=Trey Lyles bids farewell to Real Madrid|date=June 23, Until his sophomore year in high school, he had trained in the United States developmental pipeline.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/features/trey-lyles-high-school-basketball/|publisher=[[SLAM Magazine]]|author=Jones, Ryan|title=No Lie|date=September 25, 2013|access-date=October 10, 2014}} On the international stage, Lyles played for Canada's junior men's national team.{{cite web| title = Trey Lyles| publisher = Canada Basketball| url = http://www.basketball.ca/trey-lyles-p150939| access-date = August 5, 2014| archive-date = September 23, 2015| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150923182659/http://www.basketball.ca/trey-lyles-p150939| url-status = dead}} During the summer of 2013, Lyles, along with [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]], led Canada to a 6th-place finish at the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] with Lyles coming in second to Ennis in scoring at the tournament.
